maya_cs: Quick heads-up: onboarding customer 'Aurora' reporting intermittent 429s during their Node SDK warmup (200 parallel sessions). Can someone take a look?

kevin_prod: Logs show a cluster of errors around 2026-03-24T09:40:02Z: 
```
[2026-03-24T09:40:02Z] svc=aurora client=frontend auth=ok token_age=1s status=200
[2026-03-24T09:40:02Z] svc=aurora client=frontend auth=failed error=insufficient_quota
[2026-03-24T09:40:02Z] svc=aurora client=frontend status=429 message="rate limit exceeded"
```
Init snippet: 
```
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
client.preflight(); // called on every session start
```

jon_engineer: Classic preflight stampede. Two immediate mitigations: (1) cache preflight per-process for 30-60s, (2) add splay/random jitter before preflight when ramping. Also avoid ephemeral token per-request.

maya_cs: Could you add a tiny code suggestion we can share?

jon_engineer: Sure — share this minimal pattern: 
```
let pfCache = {ts:0, res:null};
async function getPreflight(){
 if(Date.now()-pfCache.ts<45000) return pfCache.res;
 await sleep(Math.random()*300+50);
 pfCache = {ts:Date.now(), res: await client.preflight()};
 return pfCache.res;
}
```

ops-bot: Alert: key=rw_live_xxxx triggered onboarding-throttle at 2026-03-24T09:40:02Z. 120s window peak_rps=58 avg_rps=14. Recommend reduce concurrency or request a short warmup bump.

kevin_prod: Implemented caching (45s) + splay + lowered parallelism to 20. Local canary shows 429s dropped from ~28% to <3%.

maya_cs: I'll open a quick support ticket if they need a temporary bump above 20. jon_engineer, can you review if they should use a short-lived session token vs per-request ephemeral?

jon_engineer: Use session-scoped ephemeral tokens during onboarding. If they expect sustained >50 rps advise Dedicated/reserved warmup or file for a temporary quota increase.

kevin_prod: Running gradual ramp now. Posting ticket id once submitted. Thanks all!
